title: Meet your open strings
summary: Learn the open strings in your selected tuning.
goal: Play the two outer open strings with a rest between attacks.
body:
No fretting experience is needed. Start at 60 BPM, or 40 BPM for more time. The outer strings do not necessarily share a pitch name or an octave relationship in a custom tuning. Listen for quiet rests: the assessment checks attacks and pitch, not how long every note rings.

Tuning: {{tuning}}. Strings 6 → 1: {{openStrings}}. Reference A4 = {{reference}} Hz. Select your actual tuning in Settings → Instrument or in Tuner. Changing the profile updates this lesson; it does not physically tune the guitar.

In the steps, {{openExample}} (6/0) means sounding note {{openExample}}, string 6, fret 0. String 1 is the thinnest; 0 means open. Read the displayed positions for your selected tuning. Pitch labels use chromatic enharmonic names. Audio measures audible pitch and attacks, not your finger or string choice.

Use a clean input from your guitar interface, or choose the acoustic microphone/pickup source explicitly. Play one note at a time and stop the previous string. Choose Practice for a signal check and count-in. Without reliable calibration, rhythm and overall scores remain unavailable. Review measured pitch or missed-attack feedback before increasing the tempo.

hear-low-e.title: 1. Hear string 6
hear-low-e.body: On beat 1, pluck the thickest open string once. {{positions}}.

leave-space.title: 2. Leave a beat of silence
leave-space.body: Beat 2 is a rest. Gently stop the low string and keep counting without a new attack.

hear-high-e.title: 3. Hear string 1
hear-high-e.body: On beat 3, pluck the thinnest open string. {{positions}}.

play-the-bar.title: 4. Play the four beats
play-the-bar.body: Count 1, 2, 3, 4: string 6, rest, string 1, rest. Notes: {{positions}}.
